I made a boat, I made a town,  I searched the caverns up and down,  And named them one and all. arxiv-2201-01316.title: Simulating Jellyfish Galaxies: A Case Study for a Gas-Rich Dwarf Galaxy
arxiv-2201-01316.creator: Jaehyun Lee, Taysun Kimm, Jérémy Blaizot, Harley Katz, Wonki Lee, Yun-Kyeong Sheen, Julien Devriendt, Adrianne Slyz
arxiv-2201-01316.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jaehyun Lee, Taysun Kimm, Jérémy Blaizot, Harley Katz, Wonki Lee, Yun-Kyeong Sheen, Julien Devriendt, Adrianne Slyz. We investigate the formation of jellyfish galaxies using radiation-hydrodynamic simulations of gas-rich dwarf galaxies with a multi-phase interstellar medium (ISM). We find that the ram-pressure-stripped (RPS) ISM is the dominant source of molecular clumps in the near wake within 10 kpc from the galactic plane, while in-situ formation is the major channel for dense gas in the distant tail of the gas-rich galaxy.

arxiv-2205-05507.title: TextMatcher: Cross-Attentional Neural Network to Compare Image and Text
arxiv-2205-05507.creator: Valentina Arrigoni, Luisa Repele, Dario Marino Saccavino
arxiv-2205-05507.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Valentina Arrigoni, Luisa Repele, Dario Marino Saccavino. We study a multimodal-learning problem where, given an image containing a single-line (printed or handwritten) text and a candidate text transcription, the goal is to assess whether the text represented in the image corresponds to the candidate text.

arxiv-2311-10374.title: Downlink Transmission in FBMC-based Massive MIMO with Co-located and Distributed Antennas
arxiv-2311-10374.creator: Hamed Hosseiny, Arman Farhang, Behrouz Farhang-Boroujeny
arxiv-2311-10374.description: Abstract This paper introduces a practical precoding method for the downlink of Filter Bank Multicarrier-based (FBMC-based) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. The proposed method comprises a two-stage precoder, consisting of a fractionally spaced prefilter (FSP) per subcarrier to equalize the channel across each subcarrier band.

arxiv-2408-07502.title: Work and Activation in a Nematic Polymer Network Ribbon
arxiv-2408-07502.creator: Harmeet Singh, Krishnan Suryanarayanan, Epifanio G. Virga
arxiv-2408-07502.description: Abstract We study spontaneous deformations of a ribbon made of nematic polymer networks and activated under the action of a mechanical load. We show that when such ribbons are activated appropriately, the deformations produced can pull back and perform work against the externally applied load.

arxiv-2503-15482.title: Natural Quantization of Neural Networks
arxiv-2503-15482.creator: Richard Barney, Djamil Lakhdar-Hamina, Victor Galitski
arxiv-2503-15482.description: Abstract We propose a natural quantization of a standard neural network, where the neurons correspond to qubits and the activation functions are implemented via quantum gates and measurements. The simplest quantized neural network corresponds to applying single-qubit rotations, with the rotation angles being dependent on the weights and measurement outcomes of the previous layer.

arxiv-2506-07862.title: Supermodulation-driven evolution of the nodal structure of bismuth-based cuprate superconductors
arxiv-2506-07862.creator: M. R. Norman
arxiv-2506-07862.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by M. R. Norman. Recent work has shown novel properties of twisted cuprates. In this paper, I point out that related phenomena occur intrinsically in bismuth-based cuprate superconductors due to the presence of the BiO supermodulation. As the ratio of the supermodulation potential to the superconducting energy gap increases, two critical points are found where semi-Dirac nodes form (that is, that have quadratic dispersion in one direction and liner dispersion in the orthogonal direction).

arxiv-2508-06409.title: A New Lens on Homelessness: Daily Tent Monitoring with 311 Calls and Street Images
arxiv-2508-06409.creator: Wooyong Jung 1, Sola Kim 2, Dongwook Kim 2, Maryam Tabar 3, Dongwon Lee 1
arxiv-2508-06409.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wooyong Jung 1, Sola Kim 2, Dongwook Kim 2, Maryam Tabar 3, Dongwon Lee 1. Homelessness in the United States has surged to levels unseen since the Great Depression. However, existing methods for monitoring it, such as point-in-time (PIT) counts, have limitations in terms of frequency, consistency, and spatial detail. This study proposes a new approach using publicly available, crowdsourced data, specifically 311 Service Calls and street-level imagery, to track and forecast homeless tent trends in San Francisco.

arxiv-2508-17357.title: Hamiltonian actions on 0 0 -shifted cosymplectic groupoids
arxiv-2508-17357.creator: Daniel López-Garcia and Fabricio Valencia
arxiv-2508-17357.description: Abstract . We introduce the notion of 0-shifted cosymplectic structure on differentiable stacks and develop a corresponding moment map theory for Hamiltonian cosymplectic actions. We present a reduction procedure, establish a version of the Kirwan convexity theorem, and obtain examples of Morse–Bott Lie groupoid morphisms. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 53D20, 57R30, 58H05 1.

arxiv-2510-13866.title: FFT-Accelerated Auxiliary Variable MCMC for Fermionic Lattice Models: A Determinant-Free Approach with O ⁡ ( N ​ log ⁡ N ) O(N\log N) Complexity
arxiv-2510-13866.creator: Deqian Kong, Shi Feng, Jianwen Xie, Ying Nian Wu
arxiv-2510-13866.description: Abstract We introduce a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm that dramatically accelerates the simulation of quantum many-body systems, a grand challenge in computational science. State-of-the-art methods for these problems are severely limited by O ⁡ ( N 3 ) O(N^{3}) computational complexity.

arxiv-2602-16395.title: Accretion Disk Magnetic Braking
arxiv-2602-16395.creator: Kurt Liffman
arxiv-2602-16395.description: Abstract A protostellar disk is threaded by a static magnetic field that is perpendicular to the disk-surface. The magnetic field acts to brake the protostellar disk and cause the disk material to move towards the protostar. General analytic equations are derived for the accretion speed, and mass accretion rate.

pmc-11550254.title: Exploring the Impact of Sex and Gender in Brain Function: Implications and Considerations
pmc-11550254.creator: Roberta Gualtierotti, Cinzia Bressi, Barbara Garavaglia, Paolo Brambilla
pmc-11550254.description: IntroductionSex and gender are crucial variables in understanding brain development and disease. Biological sex is determined by genetic and hormonal factors, whereas gender is a multidimensional construct shaped by social and cultural influences. The interplay of these factors contributes to sex-specific susceptibilities and disease progression in psychiatric and neurological disorders.

pmc-12450045.creator: Debjyoti Ghosh, Yijie Shi, Iris M. Zimmermann, Katja Holzhauser, Martin von Bergen, Anne‐Kristin Kaster, Sandra Spielvogel, Michaela A. Dippold, Jochen A. Müller, Nico Jehmlich
pmc-12450045.description: Increasing drought frequency poses a significant threat to agricultural productivity. A promising strategy to enhance crop resilience against drought is the utilisation of root channels left by winter cover crops, which can improve access to subsoil water and nutrients for subsequent cash crops like maize ( Zea mays L.).

pmc-12681768.title: The pediatric ocular surface microbiome in pet-owning households
pmc-12681768.creator: Xiangtian Ling, Charlene C Yim, Qihang Sun, Yu Peng, Yuzhou Zhang, Ka Wai Kam, Alvin L Young, Patrick Ip, Stephen Kwok-Wing Tsui, Clement C Tham, Chi Pui Pang, Li Jia Chen, Jason C Yam
pmc-12681768.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Highlights•Microbial diversity increases on ocular surfaces in children with pet exposure.•Ocular diversity is dose-dependent on daily pet-contact time.•Pet-exposed children harbor more diverse environmental and animal-related bacteria.•Ocular microbiota reveals a novel link between pet exposure and immune regulation.Keywords: Pet exposure, Ocular surface microbiome, Pediatric ophthalmology, Microbial diversity

Introduction

Pet ownership is associated with both beneficial and adverse health outcomes in children, (Friedmann and Son, 2009) including enhanced immune tolerance and reduced risk of allergic diseases, as well as potential exposure to zoonotic pathogens.

pmc-13068515.creator: Bülent Özlek
pmc-13068515.description: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and hypertension frequently coexist and together amplify cardiovascular risk, yet risk stratification in OSA remains largely centered on desaturation metrics. pmc-13185221.title: Return‐to‐play timing and secondary anterior cruciate ligament injury risk in elite soccer players: A transfermarkt‐based longitudinal analysis
pmc-13185221.creator: Riccardo D'Ambrosi, Andy Williams, Bertrand Sonnery‐Cottet, Christian Fink, Philipp Baumert
pmc-13185221.description: PurposeAnterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries are frequent and potentially career‐threatening in elite soccer. The optimal timing for return‐to‐play (RTP) remains debated, particularly its association with secondary ACL injury. This study evaluated temporal trends in RTP duration and investigated the association between RTP duration, post‐ACL match exposure and secondary ACL injury risk in professional male soccer players.

pmc-13421408.title: Tryptophan metabolism in liver transplantation immune tolerance
pmc-13421408.creator: Wei Li, Ao Ren
pmc-13421408.description: Liver transplantation is a life-saving treatment for end-stage liver disease, but long-term outcomes are limited by complications of lifelong immunosuppression. Inducing immune tolerance has become a major research priority. Tryptophan (Trp) metabolism, particularly the kynurenine pathway, is a key endogenous regulator of peripheral tolerance. This review moves beyond a simple description of metabolic routes and provides a critical, integrated analysis.

pmc-13541988.description: PurposeChildren with Hirschsprung disease (HD) frequently experience persistent bowel dysfunction after definitive surgery.
